frontmatter.title: Spatial and temporal completeness of methane satellite observations for the analysis of extreme events related to large episodic releases

children.value: Production date: 23-04-2025
🌍 Use case: Detecting extreme release of methane into the atmosphere

children.label: 🌍 Use case: Detecting extreme release of methane into the atmosphere

children.value: ❓ Quality assessment question
Are methane satellite observations suitable for detecting atmospheric signals associated with extreme emission releases?
How well, in terms of completeness, do Level 2 mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: columns capture the spatial variability of methane associated with large release events?
Methane (CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: ) is the second most important anthropogenic greenhouse gas after carbon dioxide (CO

children.html: 2_22​

children.value: ), representing about 19% of the total radiative forcing by long-lived greenhouse gases
. Atmospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: also adversely affects human health as a precursor of tropospheric ozone
. Thus, sudden large release of CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: into the atmosphere could have significant consequences in terms of climate change and health.
On 26 September 2022, multiple gas leaks were detected from the Nord Stream, an offshore submerged pipeline system that carries natural gas from Russian facilities into Western Europe (
In this application, the Level-2 mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: columns from the IASI instruments (dataset version 10.2) is evaluated. A Level 2 dataset corresponds to data from a specific combination of satellite sensor and retrivial algorithm for each individual satellite footprint along the orbit tracks (see
Although the CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: satellite observations provided by the Climate Data Store are not specifically designed to identify sudden large release events, this application explores the possibility that mid-tropospheric satellite IASI CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: (v10.2) data can be used to identify the atmospheric signal of emissions as those associated with the Nord Stream event.
📢 Quality assessment statement
These are the key outcomes of this assessment
The IASI CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: (v10.2) mid-tropospheric product was only able to partially detect the atmospheric signal of massive CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: release associated with the Nord Stream leak on September 2022.
In terms of completeness, the ability of IASI CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: (v10.2) mid-tropospheric product to detect the atmospheric signal of the CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: plume was mostly limited by the cloud coverage and users need to be aware about the strict cloud screening adopted for the production of this dataset.
As the vertical sensitivity of CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: can affect the quantification of the atmospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: signal associated with surface releases, users must be aware of the vertical sensitivity of the product. They should consult the the Documentation (e.g.,
) for information about the altitude sensitivity of the retrieved CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: The use of this data product to investigate CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: fluxes occurring at the Earth’s surface is recommended in conjunction with appropriate (inversion) modelling.
Since this dataset is updated on a yearly basis, users interested in near real time applications should consider other Copernicus resources (e.g.,
The figure shows mid-tropospheric IASI column average CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: (ppb) for 26–28 September 2022 as provided by
under CC-BY license. Turquoise boxes show regions characterised by the presence of the methane plume. AM (PM) indicate the morning (evening) satellite overpasses of each day
📋 Methodology
This notebook has three main objectives:
To compare the spatial fields of mid-tropospheric column-averaged methane (CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: ) mixing ratios from IASI sensors with independent analyses
over the geographical region and time frame (26-28 September 2022) affected by the Nord Stream emissions.
To attribute the observed differences as a function of the cloud cover over the observation scene and the adopted averaging kernels (describing the vertical sensitivity of the retrieved products).
To guide the user in the correct use of the evaluated data sets.
The analysis methodology is divided into the following steps:
1. Choose the data to use and setup the code
Define the libraries to be used.
Define notebook setup parameters and data requests.
Define the functions used in the analysis.
2. Data retrieval
Download mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: and cloud cover data for the time period and spatial region of interest.
3. Analyses and plotting
Spatial and temporal analysis of mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

Analysis of the altitude sensitivity of the retrieved mid-tropospheric CH

Note that prior to the analyses, the original Level 2 mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: data were regridded to a regular 1° x 1° grid and the cloud cover data were retrieved from the Climate Data Store dataset
“Cloud properties global gridded monthly and daily data from 1979 to present derived from satellite observations” (CLARA-A3).

As described by
, the CH

The area of high CH

as affected by the Nord Stream release over [0°-5° E, 60° - 65°N] is well visible in the IASI-C data on 28 September 2022 and partially detected by IASI-B over the western Scandinavian coasts. However, despite
, the Climate Data Store mid-tropospheric CH

children.value: data from the IASI-B and IASI-C were not able to detect the Nord Stream plume over the Baltic Sea on 26 September 2022 and west of 0°E on 28 September 2022. This is related to the fact that the Climate Data Store mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.value: columns have a lower spatial occurrence of valid data, due to the different algorithm and quality control screening applied in the dataset production.

children.value: The vertical sensitivity of the IASI CH

children.value: mid-tropospheric product may affect the identification and the quantification of the plume from the Nord Stream pipelines. The averaging kernel (AK), which is provided as variable in the Climate Data Store data, accounts for the vertical sensitivity of the derived CH

For the Climate Data Store mid-tropospheric CH

# Setting plot view
plot_kwargs = {"col": "time", "col_wrap": 1}

for sensor, da_sensor in ds[vertical_profile].groupby("sensor"):
    da_mean = diagnostics.spatial_weighted_mean(da_sensor)
    da_std = diagnostics.spatial_weighted_std(da_sensor)
    da = xr.concat(
        [
            da_mean.expand_dims(label=["mean"]),
            (da_mean + da_std).expand_dims(label=["mean $+$ std"]),
            (da_mean - da_std).expand_dims(label=["mean $-$ std"]),
        ],
        "label",
    )
    da_filtered = da.sel(time=selected_days_AK)
    facet = da_filtered.plot(
        y="pressure_weight",
        hue="label",
        yscale="log",
        yincrease=False,
        ylim=(1000, 10),  # Limit y axis to 1
        **plot_kwargs,
    )
    for ax in facet.axs.flatten():
        ax.grid()
    plt.suptitle(f"{sensor = }", y=1.01)
    plt.show()

To illustrate that the use of this dataset without appropriate modelling can lead to misleading conclusions, we analysed the temporal variability of the mid-tropospheric CH

children.html: 4_44​

children.html: 4_44​

children.value:
values for each single day during September 2022 for both IASI-B and IASI-C. The box and wiskers plot shows the percentiles of the data distribution, the median (green line) as well as the outliers.
It can be seen that despite the occurrence of the Nord Stream leak and the effective detection of the plume signal by IASI-C on 29 September 2022, the CH

children.value: values did not deviate from the monthly variability. This shows that even if the atmospheric data provided by the mid-tropospheric IASI CH

children.value: release from the Nord Stream pipelines, it can hardly be detected without the use of appropriate modelling, as adopted by
